evidence.claim: For QSR operators, realistic broadline distribution choices in many markets are described as limited to Sysco, US Foods, or Performance Food Group, with distributors influencing delivery schedules, minimum order quantities, payment terms, and product availability.
evidence.source_title: QSR Supply Chain: How Sysco, US Foods, PFG Control Food Distribution 2026 | QSR Pro

evidence.claim: The same QSR supply-chain source states that small operators can face stockouts, substitutions, minimum-order burdens, and shorter payment terms, while large chains can negotiate better terms.
evidence.source_title: QSR Supply Chain: How Sysco, US Foods, PFG Control Food Distribution 2026 | QSR Pro

evidence.claim: Franchisors can negotiate master supply agreements with food distributors, equipment manufacturers, and service providers, and franchisees may be required to purchase from approved vendors.
evidence.source_title: Behind the Curtain: How QSR Supply Chain Contracts Are Squeezing Franchisees | QSR Pro

evidence.claim: Federal franchise disclosure rules require franchisors to disclose certain supplier relationships, including required purchases, approved suppliers, and whether the franchisor receives rebates or other compensation from vendors.
evidence.source_title: Behind the Curtain: How QSR Supply Chain Contracts Are Squeezing Franchisees | QSR Pro

evidence.claim: Specialty B2B ingredient companies support foodservice operators by solving formulation, consistency, scalability, menu innovation, and labor-saving challenges.
evidence.source_title: Specialty B2B Ingredients: Foodservice Industry Outlook - Lincoln International LLC

evidence.claim: Lincoln International describes specialty B2B ingredient companies as developing durable and sticky customer relationships across the foodservice channel because restaurants often lack the time, labor, and infrastructure to develop complex formulations internally.
evidence.source_title: Specialty B2B Ingredients: Foodservice Industry Outlook - Lincoln International LLC

evidence.claim: Black Rock Coffee Bar reported 181 locations across seven states as of December 31, 2025, and described a fully company-owned, drive-thru-led specialty coffee platform with proprietary Fuel energy drinks and a loyalty program.
evidence.source_title: Black Rock Coffee Bar details growth and 2025 IPO | BRCB Annual Report (10-K)

evidence.claim: Black Rock Coffee Bar disclosed that proprietary Fuel energy drinks generated about 24% of 2025 revenue and loyalty accounted for roughly 63% of 2025 sales, while the company remained unprofitable and disclosed risks around growth execution, supply chain, labor, leverage, and governance.
evidence.source_title: Black Rock Coffee Bar details growth and 2025 IPO | BRCB Annual Report (10-K)

memory_update.text: FCPT should remain in the underfollowed lane as a restaurant-focused net-lease proxy until latest filings verify tenant mix, rent coverage, acquisition cap rates, lease escalators, and casual-dining/QSR split.
NNN should be treated as a diluted second-order restaurant real-estate exposure, not a pure restaurant ticker, unless filings show meaningful restaurant tenant concentration.
DOOR is a reference node for restaurant customer access, delivery economics, and merchant-margin pressure rather than an underfollowed candidate.

MCD, YUM, SBUX, CMG, WING, CAVA, and TXRH are reference benchmarks for demand, unit economics, franchise health, commodity sensitivity, labor productivity, and supplier anchoring; they should not crowd out second-order suppliers and service providers.
Need latest 10-K/10-Q and investor supplement verification for every candidate in this chunk before upgrading company-level claims above hypothesis or inference.
Need direct restaurant tenant and rent-coverage disclosures for FCPT and NNN to determine whether restaurant real estate is a real chokepoint exposure or merely a thematic overlay.

Need cross-company evidence on restaurant delivery commission pressure and first-party digital ordering to evaluate whether DOOR is a chokepoint, a demand generator, or a margin headwind for restaurant operators.
Need supplier and procurement mapping for MCD, YUM, SBUX, CMG, WING, CAVA, BROS, and TXRH to discover smaller public suppliers hidden behind reference restaurant brands.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into restaurant-theme ticker relationships. The chunk splits into two lanes: reference leaders that benchmark demand, franchise economics, digital/customer-access, and commodity sensitivity; and underfollowed second-order names where restaurant economics are embedded in real estate, franchise financing, or regional drive-thru beverage expansion. Evidence is currently strongest for broad theme mechanics: consolidated foodservice distribution, franchise approved-vendor economics, specialty B2B ingredient stickiness, and drive-thru beverage disclosure from Black Rock Coffee Bar. Direct ticker-level evidence for FCPT, NNN, BROS, CAVA, TXRH, WING, CMG, SBUX, YUM, MCD, and DOOR still requires latest 10-K/10-Q and investor presentation verification before upgrading claims.
